claims.text: The as-deposited Fe25Ni21Mn24Si13Ge17 alloy is amorphous or extremely fine/disordered and has cubic-type short-range order.
The studied nanoribbon arrays have 1 µm ribbon spacing and a thickness of 35 nm.
Annealing at 700 K induces short-range atomic reordering in the amorphous alloy.
Annealing at 700 K relieves fabrication-induced internal strain.
The proposed 700 K anneal preserves the amorphous matrix and cubic-type short-range order without bulk crystallization.
Annealing-induced reordering and strain relaxation reduce local domain-pinning barriers or sites.
Reduced domain pinning and short-range reordering improve cooperative ferromagnetic exchange and increase the effective ferromagnetic volume.
The annealing-induced magnetic changes increase the low-field magnetocaloric spin-entropy change.
The proposed enhancement preserves rapid heat exchange and mechanical stability.
Elastic longitudinal tensile strain up to 2% enhances magnetoelastic coupling above 100 K.
Strain-induced magnetoelastic anisotropy reinforces or stabilizes magnetic order above 100 K.
Applying elastic strain up to 2% does not shift the magnetic-cluster blocking peak.
Applying elastic strain up to 2% does not induce or disrupt in-plane magnetic anisotropy.
The as-deposited baseline has a maximum conventional −ΔSM of approximately 1.25 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 140 K under a 50 kOe field change.
Relative to the as-deposited baseline, 700 K annealing increases saturation magnetization.
Relative to the as-deposited baseline, 700 K annealing increases the maximum −ΔSM.
Elastic strain produces a stronger magnetic response above 100 K than in the unstrained baseline.
Full crystallization occurs at or above approximately 1000 K.
The hypothesized behavior is limited to the metastable non-crystalline state, 1 µm-spaced nanoribbons, and elastic strains from 0% to 2%.
